post.summary: `POST /api/v1/pair` — redeem the live pairing code for a device token.
post.description:
Every failed redemption (a wrong code, a spent one, an expired one, none
live) answers the same `403 pairing_refused`, so a guesser learns nothing
about the host's state from the answer. A body that holds no code at all is
`400 bad_request` and costs no attempt: it is judged before the pairing is
read. The token rides this one response and no log line.

201.description: the device is paired; the token rides this one response

403.description: the code did not pair a device (`pairing_refused`)

get.summary: `GET /api/v1/panes` — every herdr pane with the tollgate sessions inside it.
get.description:
Joined on process ids, never on the `tokens.tollgate` tag. Herdr absent
answers 200 with `present: false`, the one fixed sentence naming the state,
and no panes — never an error. At most `1 + N` herdr calls at 2 s each,
where `N` is the pane count.

200.description: every herdr pane on this host with the tollgate sessions running inside it, joined on process ids (the foreground process group leader is the pane's own session, as is a listed `tollgate` running `start` or `resume` under a wrapper; any other listed process is a delegate; the display tag never joins; on Windows herdr lists only the pane's agent root, so no session joins there); at most 1 + N herdr calls at 2 s each

get.summary: `GET /api/v1/sessions` — a page of the transcript index, newest first.
get.description:
The walk lists every transcript from filenames and mtimes alone, the cursor
and limit cut the page, and only the rows on it are previewed (a bounded

get.summary:
`GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}` — a page of one transcript's records, paged
backward from the file's end by byte offset.
get.description:
The id is looked up among the stems the walk yields, never joined onto a
store path, so an id spelled as a path can only answer 404. The page is
bounded by records and by bytes ([`PAGE_MAX_BYTES`]), and a record longer
than the byte bound is served alone, never cut.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: the session id: the transcript filename stem, as the listing's `id` and a pane's `agent_session_id` name it

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: the `next_before` of an earlier page, a byte offset; absent for the newest page

200.description: the last records whose lines end at or before the cursor, oldest first, each one Claude Code transcript record verbatim; at most 4 MiB of records unless the page's one record is larger

get.description:
Served straight off disk in the common case. The main loop already rewrites
that file atomically every tick, so passing the bytes through takes no lock,
duplicates no serialization, and cannot drift from the documented schema.
`?all=1` and a missing file both fall back to building a body here, which is
the same `build_status` the file itself came from.

Conditional, and optionally BLOCKING: `?wait=` with a matching
`If-None-Match` holds the request open until the feed's content actually
changes. That is what turns a client's account display from
"correct within its poll interval" into "correct within a round trip", and
with `POST /api/v1/switch` republishing the file itself, a switch made through
the API wakes every waiting reader immediately.

`?all=1` never waits: it builds its body from config rather than the file,
so there is no file to watch for it — but it is still conditional off its
built body's tag, so a roster that has not moved answers 304.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: hold the request until the feed changes, at most 60 seconds, only with a matching If-None-Match

parameters.name: If-None-Match
parameters.description: an `ETag` from an earlier answer; a match answers 304 or, with `wait`, holds the request

post.description:
A thin wrapper over [`switch_profile_noninteractive`], the same action the
MCP `switch` tool calls. That is deliberate and load-bearing: the AUTH-1
gate (never install credentials a refresh has rejected), the disabled-target
refusal, and the divergence policy all live inside it, so this endpoint
cannot drift into a weaker switch than the rest of tollgate performs.

500.description: the device list does not read (`internal`), or the switch failed (`switch_failed`)

AccountObservation.description:
Everything tollgate can say about one account at read time.

Core fields always serialise (an absent `Option` is `null`, an empty list
is `[]`). Additive health and note fields are omitted when absent.

id.description:
Stable account id, `<namespace>:<name>`:
`claude:<profile>` (a `profiles.toml` profile of any provider),
`codex:<profile>` (a `codex-profiles.toml` profile),
`monitor:<id>` (a monitoring-only account with no profile — an
unbound management key, an Ollama monitor key),
`upstream:<profile>` (an account upstream clauth owns, read-only),
`hermes:<profile>` (a `hermes-profiles.toml` Hermes home).
Build it with [`account_id`].

label.description: Human name: the profile name, or a monitor's configured label.

provider.description:
Provider display name (`Anthropic`, `OpenRouter`, `OpenAI`), from
[`SourceId::display_name`] unless the producer knows better.

plan.description:
The plan / tier label (`Max 5x`, `plus`, `pro-legacy`), provider value
first, else a user-configured label; `None` when neither exists.

active.description:
This account is the one the harness is using now (the global active
profile of its roster).

disabled.description: The operator disabled this profile (hidden from the chain and polling).

endpoint.description:
The inference endpoint for an api-key account, `None` for a
first-party subscription. Never carries a credential.

freshness.description:
How current the figures are. Separate from [`Self::failure`]: stale
figures stay visible (plan §3.2).

oneOf.description: The last known reason the account cannot be read or cannot serve.

windows.description: Quota windows, lead-first where the source knows an order.

money.description: Money meters: balances, spend, caps, budgets.

oneOf.description: A local cost estimate, only when attribution is exact.

banked_resets.description:
Banked early-reset passes the account can spend (codex
`rate_limit_reset_credits`); `None` when the source has no such thing.

best_effort.description:
The figures come from a best-effort scanner rather than a typed
integration; readers should say so.

oneOf.description:
When the provider produced the figures shown (the fetch that wrote the
cache). `None` when nothing dates them.

When tollgate last TRIED to read the account, successful or not. Only a
live scheduler knows this; cache readers leave it `None`.

AgentOk.description: The answer both routes carry once herdr accepted the request.

Amount.description:
An exact, signed decimal amount of money.

**Representation: the canonical decimal string** (`"13.67"`, `"-5.71"`,
`"0.000123456789"`), not integer micro-units. Providers hand money over as
decimal strings (DeepSeek, Nous, Ollama `activity.cost`) or as JSON numbers
with more than six fractional digits (OpenRouter per-request spend), and
micro-units would round both; a string carries whatever precision arrived.
It is also the JSON shape money APIs use, so `usage --json` readers get a
string they can hand to their own decimal type.

Canonical form: optional `-`, the integer digits with no leading zeros
(`"0"` for none), then `.` and the fractional digits exactly as given
(trailing zeros kept — `"1132.60"` stays `"1132.60"`). A zero is never
negative. Comparison ([`Ord`], [`PartialEq`]) is NUMERIC, so `"1.5"` equals
`"1.50"`; the string is kept as given for display fidelity.

Deserialises from a JSON string or number; always serialises as a string.

Answerer.description:
What answered `/health` on the bind port of a [`GatewayState::Foreign`]
gateway.

ChainOrderOk.description:
The answer a successful reorder carries: the canonical member names in the
new order.

ChainThresholdOk.description:
The answer a successful threshold edit carries: the canonical profile name
and the stored value.

ChainWrapOffOk.description: The answer a successful wrap-off edit carries.

ErrorBody.description:
One error body for every refused or failed answer, so a client generates a
single error shape. `reason` rides only the refusals that carry one —
today's `error()` answers have no `reason` key at all — so it is skipped
when `None`, never serialized as `null`.

code.description: The exit code, `null` for a process a signal ended.

signal.description:
The signal that ended it, `null` for an exit code (and always on
Windows).

Failure.description: Why an account cannot be read, or cannot serve.

message.description:
One human sentence, passed through [`sanitize_message`] — never a raw
provider body, never a credential.

oneOf.description: When a retry can succeed (a 429's `retry-after`), when known.

Fallback.description:
The `fallback` object for a profile: chain membership (`position` is
1-based), the utilization threshold auto-switch rotates away at, and whether
this member is currently armed (`armed` = in the chain AND active). Field
order is the published key order.

oneOf.description: Read within the source's staleness threshold.

Past the threshold (or undatable). `since` is when the shown figures
were read; `None` when nothing dates them.
Nothing has ever been read.

Freshness.description:
How current an observation's figures are. `{"state": "fresh"}`,
`{"state": "stale", "since": "…"}`, `{"state": "not_fetched"}`.

GatewaySlot.description:
The `gateway` slot: `status.json`'s top-level object and the body of
`GET /api/v1/gateway`. Paths, a port, a pid, versions and states only:
never an env value, a token or a file's content.

config.description: The adopted config, `null` with no record.

binary.description:
The binary the gateway runs as: the record's path, else `shunt`,
looked up on `PATH`.

port.description: The port the gateway binds, or the port a foreign answerer holds.

pid.description: The pid of the gateway tollgate spawned, while one runs.

version.description:
The version `/health` reported: tollgate's gateway's, or a shunt-shaped
foreign answerer's.

oneOf.description: What answered on the port of a `foreign` gateway.

restarts.description:
Restarts after an exit tollgate did not ask for, since the daemon
started.

oneOf.description: How the last gateway process ended, `null` before any has.

since.description:
ISO-8601 UTC stamp of when `state` last changed; `null` without a
supervisor.

GatewayState.description: The managed gateway's state, a closed set.

HealthBody.description:
`GET /api/v1/health` — the build's version and the feed schema, so a client
refuses a daemon newer than it knows.

HerdrState.description:
What this route knows about herdr itself. `reason` is the one fixed sentence
naming the absent state, omitted when herdr is present.

HermesProfileEntry.description:
One Hermes profile in `status.json` (hermes spec D-H12). There is no
`active_hermes_profile`: Hermes has no global slot, and a Hermes home is
launched by name.

model.description: The model passed as `-m` at launch, when the roster sets one.

live.description: A `tollgate start` (or `hermes auth`) holds the home now.

records.description: The page's records in file order, oldest first.

next_before.description:
The `before` of the page of older records, `null` when nothing older
remains.

malformed.description:
Lines in the page's range that were not a JSON object (a torn last line
mid-write, a blank line), skipped rather than served.

HistoryRecord.description: One record of a transcript page.

offset.description: The byte offset the record's line starts at.

record.description: One Claude Code transcript record, verbatim.

KeyHealthState.description: The latest API-key health check, independent of quota or spend figures.

LocalEstimate.description:
A local cost estimate (token ledger × price table), only when every token
is attributable to this account.

basis.description: One phrase naming the inputs (`token ledger × ai-pricelog`).

ModelCount.description: Requests made to one model inside a window.

MoneyMeter.description:
One money figure.

`amount` semantics depend on `kind`:
- `balance`: what is left to spend (negative = debt). `limit` = the pool's
  size when the source publishes one.
- `spend`: what was spent in `period`. `limit` = the cap on that spend.
- `limit`: what is LEFT under a cap (`limit_remaining`); `limit` = the cap.
- `budget`: a user-configured budget's remaining amount; `limit` = the budget.

scope_id.description:
Provider id of the scope (org / account), for de-dup. `None` never
de-dups.

additive.description: `false` for a derived total that must never be summed with its parts.

Origin.description: Where an account is defined; also its [`AccountObservation::id`] namespace.

PairOk.description:
The answer a successful pairing carries: the device's name and tier, and the
one-time token the device keeps from here.

PaneEntry.description: One pane, in herdr's own order, with its tollgate sessions.

agent.description: The agent herdr associates with the pane, `null` when none.

cwd.description: The pane's cwd, `null` when herdr has none.

tag.description: The `tokens.tollgate` display tag, `null` when absent; never used to join.

foreground_process_group_id.description:
The pane's foreground process group, `null` when its `process-info` did
not answer (the pane closed between the two calls) or when the pane has
no foreground job.

agent_session_id.description:
The agent's own session id herdr detected in the pane (`agent_session`
of kind `id`), the id `GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}` pages; `null` when
herdr detected none.

PaneSession.description: One tollgate session running inside a pane.

profile.description:
The member the session's requests authenticate as: for an api-key hot
swap the member its key helper last served, which trails the
committed one until the session's next request; else the member the
session currently holds, else its launch profile.

state.description:
Where the session is in a switch: `requested`, `swapping` (committed,
not served yet), `stalled` (its key helper failed) or `served`.

cwd.description: The session's cwd, `null` when the row has none.

Period.description: The period a spend meter covers: `[start, end)`.

derived.description: The bounds were derived by tollgate, not published by the provider.

ProfileEntry.description:
One `profiles[]` entry of the published `status.json` body — the shape both
the writer ([`build_profile_entries`], serialized by [`build_status`]) and
the reader (`tollgate list`'s table rows) derive from, so a reader's field
access cannot drift from what the writer emits. Contract: wiki/Daemon.md.

active.description:
Active-profile marker source. The active profile is always kept, disabled
or not: the top-level `active_profile` field names it unconditionally,
and a reader resolves that name against `profiles[]`.

rolling_token.description:
Additive (CLA-ROLL): what the sidecar actually HOLDS — the same content
classification the TUI renders, not the config flag. The two part ways
exactly when honesty matters: a dead chain degrades the sidecar onto its
static mint while the flag stays on, and the flag would promise readers
a re-stamp for a mint nobody is going to re-stamp. While true, the
sidecar's hours-scale countdown is routine maintenance (daemon re-stamps
on rotation and on the freshness timer); while false it is a real
credential clock. Readers key their token-row rendering off this so a
rolling token never displays as an expiring mint — nor the reverse.

provider.description: Display provider label: a recognised third-party name, else `anthropic`.

base_url.description: The third-party endpoint, `None` for the default Anthropic one.

tier.description:
Human tier label for an anthropic account (`Max 5x`); `None` for
third-party/api-key profiles.

harness.description:
Additive (schema stays 1): which harness this profile belongs to,
`claude` or `codex`. Membership of a state file is the authority
(decision 1) and names are globally unique (decision 2), so one flat
`profiles[]` still reads unambiguously — a reader that predates codex
ignores the field and sees the claude accounts it always saw, because
codex entries are appended after them.

has_live_session.description: A live `tollgate start` session runs for this profile.

fetch_status.description:
Freshness: a live daemon's verdict or the cache-mtime derivation; `None`
when there is no cache at all.

stale.description:
Additive: true when this reading is distrusted, by
either arm — a deep-slot stuck RateLimited, or reading age past
`stale_after_ms(interval)` (the stuck arm needs the live stores and is
`false` single-shot). Readers dim it / show a "stuck" cue instead of
treating it as current truth.

next_refresh_at.description:
ISO-8601 UTC stamp of the next scheduled refresh; `None` when none is
pending (a spent skipped account, or no cache).

oneOf.description:
Additive: this profile's slot in the interleaved
auto-start queue, `None`/`null` when it holds none — the toggle is off,
it never opted into `auto_start`, or it cannot open a window.
`default` so a reader stays additive-tolerant of an older writer.

The chain-membership object (`position` / `threshold` / `armed`), `None`
when not a chain member.

windows.description:
The 5h/7d usage rows: an OAuth account's own windows, or an api-key
account's provider-derived ones. Empty when the cache behind them
holds none.

oneOf.description:
The third-party availability object (`available`), `None` for OAuth
accounts.

QueueEntry.description:
One profile's `auto_start_queue` object in `status.json`: the 1-based slot,
and the queue's shared next-open ESTIMATE — the queue gates globally, so the
stamp is when the NEXT window opens, whoever opens it, and a window opened
out of band moves it as soon as the gate takes that opening up
([`crate::usage::queue_anchor`]). `next_open_at` is `null` only when no anchor is
derivable yet (cold history); an anchored-but-due queue publishes
`anchor + gap` even once that instant is past — readers compare it to now,
exactly as wiki/Daemon.md contracts.

QuotaWindow.description: One rolling or calendar quota window.

id.description:
Stable per source: [`WINDOW_SESSION`], [`WINDOW_WEEKLY`],
`weekly:<model>`, [`WINDOW_MONTH`], or a slug of the provider's label.

used_pct.description: Share consumed, percent, UNCLAMPED; `None` when not published.

exhausted.description: The provider says (or the figure proves) this window is spent.

oneOf.description: When the window resets; `None` when the source gives no time.

window_secs.description: Nominal length, for pace; `None` for a calendar / unknown window.

chain_eligible.description: Whether today's fallback chain judges this window (the 5h / 7d fold).

used.description:
Absolute amount consumed, in the provider's own unit (tokens, calls),
when published.

limit.description: Absolute ceiling in the same unit, when published.

breakdown.description: Per-model request counts inside this window (Ollama); informational.

oneOf.description: The inference credential's own provider response.

A separate monitoring credential; `bound` once proven to be the same
account as the profile's key.
Only a user-configured label groups it; never merged.

ScopeOrigin.description:
Who vouches for a meter's scope. `{"kind": "provider"}`,
`{"kind": "monitoring_credential", "bound": true}`, `{"kind": "user_label"}`.

cwd.description: Absolute path to the directory the pane's shell starts in.

profile.description:
A tollgate profile (claude or codex roster); mutually exclusive with
`kind`. Neither means bare `claude`.

kind.description: A herdr agent kind; mutually exclusive with `profile`.

workspace.description: The herdr workspace the tab lands in, when named.

SessionCreated.description: The answer a created session carries.

agent_status.description:
herdr's `agent_status` read back after the agent call; `null` for the
`pane run` arm (a tollgate profile), whose readiness herdr detects later
and `/events` carries.

SessionKind.description: How a session's pid matched the pane.

SessionRow.description:
One row of the transcript index: the fields `tollgate sessions --json`
emits minus its `tokens`/`cost`, plus the store the transcript lives in.

id.description: The transcript filename stem, the id `GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}` pages.

last_ran_profile.description: The profile the session last ran under, `null` when unknown.

workspace.description: The `cwd` off the transcript head, empty when it records none.

first_message.description:
The first user message, redacted and cut like `tollgate sessions --json`,
`null` when the head held none.

last_message.description:
The last user message, redacted and cut the same way, `null` when the
tail held none.

store.description:
`global`, `guest` for guest mode's own store, or `isolated:<profile>`
for a live isolated run's own store.

next_before.description: The `before` of the next page, `null` when this page ends the index.

SourceId.description:
Which integration an observation's figures came from. Serialises as
[`SourceId::as_str`] (`anthropic_oauth`, `ollama_cloud`, `openrouter`, …).

StatusBody.description:
The full `status.json` body. Field order is the published key order, and
each `Option` field emits a present key holding `null` when absent.

active_codex_profile.description:
Additive per-harness slots (decision 10): the top-level
`active_profile` / `wrap_off` above stay the CLAUDE ones, so nothing
that reads them today changes meaning. `default` so a reader stays
additive-tolerant of an older writer.

tollgate_version.description:
The daemon that wrote this feed. A reader can tell an old daemon —
one with no codex support at all — from a new one reporting an empty
codex roster, which are otherwise byte-identical.

oneOf.description:
Additive: the managed shunt gateway, the object `GET /api/v1/gateway`
serves. `default` so a reader stays additive-tolerant of an older
writer.

hermes_profiles.description:
Additive: the Hermes roster. Its own list, never appended to
`profiles[]`: a Hermes home has no windows, tier or auth grade for a
`ProfileEntry` to carry. `default` so a reader stays additive-tolerant
of an older writer.

SwapState.description: Where a session is in a switch.

SwitchOk.description:
The answer a successful switch carries: the profile left behind and the one
now active. `previous` is `None` exactly when there was no active profile to
leave, which today's wire answers as `null` — so the `Option` is serialized,
never skipped.

ThirdPartyAvailability.description:
The third-party availability object (`available`), for api-key accounts
whose figures live in `third_party_cache.json`; `None` for OAuth accounts.

Timestamp.description:
A UTC instant with one-second resolution, as epoch seconds. Serialises as an
RFC 3339 string (`2026-09-29T10:00:00+00:00`, the spelling every other
tollgate feed uses via [`crate::usage::epoch_secs_to_iso`]) and parses any
RFC 3339 offset back.

Window.description:
One published window row — the `{label, utilization_pct, resets_at}`
spelling of a 5h, 7d, or per-model weekly window. Both writers
([`usage_windows`] → the daemon's `status.json` feed and the MCP payloads)
and the reader (`tollgate list`'s 5h/7d columns) derive from this one struct,
so a reader's key spelling cannot drift from what a writer emits.

oneOf.description: The account's shared pool across models (Anthropic 5h / 7d).

An account-wide counter that is not the shared pool (OpenRouter free
daily requests, a provider's 30d ceiling).
Limited to these models.
One product surface (e.g. a coding plan).
